Do not recommend untrained repairs or treat a visual check as proof of equipment safety; local availability and prices are not required.", "scoring_guidance": {"completion": "Meet all explicit time, resource, length and deliverable constraints.", "logic": "Keep assumptions, subject knowledge and dependencies coherent; acknowledge missing evidence.", "value": "Provide feasible, specific steps and checks that advance the stated goal.", "clarity": "Make the plan easy to follow for its intended facilitator or decision maker."}, "candidate_answer": "[Step 01] Define your climbing activity.
Decide whether you will climb indoors or outdoors and whether you will boulder, top-rope, lead climb, or climb trad. Confirm the location, dates, duration, and number of participants.

[Step 02] Confirm your skills and supervision needs.
Check the venue’s training, belay-test, and access requirements. If you lack the necessary skills, book a qualified instructor or guided session rather than relying on rented equipment alone.

[Step 03] Make an equipment checklist.
Ask the venue or guide what is provided and what you must rent. Depending on the activity, this may include climbing shoes, harness, helmet, belay device, locking carabiners, rope, quickdraws, or a bouldering crash pad. Have a qualified professional confirm compatibility and suitability.

[Step 04] Find suitable rental providers.
Contact climbing gyms, outdoor shops, or guide services near your destination. Confirm that they rent the required equipment and allow it to be used at your intended location.

[Step 05] Compare prices and rental terms.
Request an itemized quote covering rental duration, taxes, deposit, and any cleaning or damage charges. Check cancellation rules, late-return fees, replacement liability, and pickup and return hours.

[Step 06] Confirm availability and reserve.
Provide your dates, quantities, shoe sizes, and harness measurements. Reserve early and request written confirmation of the equipment, total price, and collection arrangements.

[Step 07] Prepare the required information and documents.
Bring the identification and payment method required by the provider, along with booking confirmation. Complete rental agreements and waivers; arrange guardian consent if required for minors.

[Step 08] Inspect and fit the equipment at pickup.
With rental staff, check for wear, damage, missing parts, and correct operation. Try on shoes, harness, and helmet. Ask about inspection records and retirement policies for safety-critical gear. Reject questionable items and document existing damage.

[Step 09] Confirm safe use and emergency arrangements.
Ask staff to demonstrate unfamiliar adjustments and explain manufacturer restrictions. Do not treat a pickup demonstration as a substitute for climbing instruction. Confirm local emergency procedures and weather-related restrictions for outdoor climbing.

[Step 10] Collect and verify the rental.
Check every item against the agreement, obtain a receipt, and confirm the exact return deadline and location. Transport equipment securely, away from chemicals, sharp objects, and excessive heat.

[Step 11] Use and care for the equipment responsibly.
Follow your training, venue rules, and manufacturer instructions. Perform appropriate pre-use and partner checks. Stop using any suspect equipment and report damage, significant loading, or chemical exposure to the provider.

[Step 12] Return the equipment and close the rental.
Return all items on time, following the provider’s cleaning and drying instructions. Report any incidents or damage, request a joint inventory check, settle any charges, and obtain confirmation of return and deposit release."}
